content.content:
===== Cp07 =====
8:/** registration-date: the effective registration date rolls off weekends to the
9: * next Monday (supplied dates too). 2026-01-03 is a Saturday -> 2026-01-05 (Mon); a weekday is kept. */
14:	void coreWeekendRollsToMonday() throws Exception {
16:		o.put("registrationDate", "2026-01-03"); // Saturday
18:		getOwner(id).andExpect(jsonPath("$.registrationDate").value("2026-01-05"));
24:		o.put("registrationDate", "2026-01-06"); // Tuesday
26:		getOwner(id).andExpect(jsonPath("$.registrationDate").value("2026-01-06"));
===== Cp14 =====
9:/** membership-number: the YY segment uses the business-day-adjusted
10: * registration date. Supplying a Saturday whose Monday roll stays in the same year, the YY still
11: * matches the returned (adjusted) registrationDate's year. */
18:		o.put("registrationDate", "2026-01-03"); // Saturday -> Monday 2026-01-05
20:		String yy = r.get("registrationDate").asText().substring(2, 4);
21:		assertTrue(r.get("membershipNumber").asText().endsWith("-M" + yy),
22:				r.get("membershipNumber").asText());
===== Cp15 =====
8:/** membership-tier: Return 'membershipTier': 'SILVER' when namesakeCount is 0 and an email is present, otherwi... */
18:		getOwner(id).andExpect(jsonPath("$.membershipTier").value("SILVER"));
24:		getOwner(id).andExpect(jsonPath("$.membershipTier").value("BRONZE"));
===== Cp19 =====
7:/** daily-limit: the create-limit counts owners per adjusted business day. All
8: * owners created now map to the same business day, so 100 creates then the 101st is rejected. */
===== Cp20 =====
10:/** business-day: the default registration date must fall on a business day (a weekend rolls
11: * forward to Monday). Can't force the server's clock black-box, so assert the invariant that holds
12: * every day: the default registrationDate is never a Saturday or Sunday. */
19:		DayOfWeek dow = LocalDate.parse(fetchOwner(id).get("registrationDate").asText()).getDayOfWeek();

## Summary

I implemented the business-day rule for the registration date in `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner` (`POST /api/owners`, the only endpoint that creates owners — V2 only exposes a paged listing).

**Changes to `OwnerRestControllerV1.java`:**

1. **Compute the effective date, then roll it to a business day, up front.** Before the daily-limit check, the effective date is taken from the request (`owner.getRegistrationDate()`) or defaulted to the server date (`LocalDate.now()`), then passed through a new `toBusinessDay(...)` helper and stored on the owner:
